tutorial.title: Stopping Functions with Return
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn how to stop functions in the middle of their execution with the help of the return statement.

lessons.title: Intro
lessons.interactiveContent: Let's learn how to use return statements to exit functions at any time we want, even in the middle of the code.

lessons.title: End of a function
lessons.interactiveContent:
We've learned to use return at the end of a function to pass a value as output.

Make sure to pick return, followed by number * 10, and finally ;.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We've learned to use return at the end of a function to pass a value as output.

Complete the line that makes multiplyByTen(29) return 290.

Make sure to pick return, followed by number * 10, and finally ;.

lessons.title: Nothing gets executed
lessons.interactiveContent:
Anything after a return statement doesn't execute. Here, the display statement after the return statement doesn't work at all.

Make sure to pick return number * 10;.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Anything after a return statement doesn't execute. Here, the display statement after the return statement doesn't work at all.

Complete the early exit so the program logs only 290.

Make sure to pick return, followed by number * 10, and finally ;.

lessons.title: Multiple return statements
lessons.interactiveContent:
If we have multiple return statements, whichever one runs first exits the function. Here, only 290 gets returned.

Make sure to pick return, followed by "This line doesn't execute", and finally ;.
lessons.hardModeContent:
If we have multiple return statements, whichever one runs first exits the function. Here, only 290 gets returned.

Complete the second return statement, which does not run because the function has already exited.

Make sure to pick return, followed by "This line doesn't execute", and finally ;.

lessons.title: Return in if statements
lessons.interactiveContent:
If we use conditional statements, we can use return to stop a function at different parts of the code based on the input.

Make sure to pick return, followed by return.
lessons.hardModeContent:
If we use conditional statements, we can use return to stop a function at different parts of the code based on the input.

For an age of 67, complete the condition that returns 50% OFF.

Make sure to pick >=, followed by 65, return, and finally "50% OFF".

lessons.title: Last return statement
lessons.interactiveContent:
Return statements at the end of the function and outside of any conditional statement are run only if no conditions have been met.

Make sure to pick return.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Return statements at the end of the function and outside of any conditional statement are run only if no conditions have been met.

For an age of 18, complete the fallback that returns 0% OFF.

Make sure to pick return, followed by "0% OFF", and finally ;.

lessons.title: Catch last case
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can use the last return statement to catch the last possible case. Here, if age is between 18 and 65, the full price is charged.

Make sure to pick return, followed by "Full price", and finally ;.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We can use the last return statement to catch the last possible case. Here, if age is between 18 and 65, the full price is charged.

Complete the final fallback so an age of 25 returns Full price.

Make sure to pick return, followed by "Full price", and finally ;.

lessons.title: Question: End of a function
lessons.interactiveContent:
Why do we use return statements?

To return a value from a functionTo display a value in the console

To return a value from a function.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We use return statements to return a value from a function.

A function calculates a total that code outside the function needs later. What should the function use?

A return statement to pass the total out of the function.A console.log statement to pass the total out of the function.A second function name to display the total.

A return statement to pass the total out of the function.

lessons.title: Question: Nothing gets executed
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens with instructions placed after a return statement?

The instructions don't execute since return stops the functionNothing, the instructions execute as normal

The instructions don't execute since return stops the function.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A function runs return total; and the next line is console.log(total);. What happens to the console line?

It does not run because return has already exited the function.It runs before the returned value is passed out.It changes the returned value to a string.

It does not run because return has already exited the function.

lessons.title: Question: Multiple return statements
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which return statement executes in this code?

return number * 10;return "This line isn't executed";

return number * 10;.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Based on the displayed function, what does console.log(result) print?

290This line isn't executed290This line isn't executed

Make sure to pick 290.

lessons.title: Question: Return in if statements
lessons.interactiveContent:
Why do we use return statements and conditional statements together?

To stop a function at different parts of its executionTo return multiple outputs simultaneously

To stop a function at different parts of its execution.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We use return statements and conditional statements to stop a function at different parts based on the input.

A function checks a condition and returns a different message when it is true. Why pair the condition with return?

To stop the function with the outcome for that case.To make every return statement run.To display multiple outcomes at once.

To stop the function with the outcome for that case.

lessons.title: Question: Last return statement
lessons.interactiveContent:
What's wrong with this code?

The last return statement is outside the functionThe condition will never be true

The last return statement is outside the function.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Look at the displayed braces and return statements. Which line causes the error?

return "Not a senior"; because it is outside the function.return "50% OFF"; because it is inside an if statement.const result = getDiscount(18); because it calls the function.

return "Not a senior"; because it is outside the function.

lessons.title: Question: Catch last case
lessons.interactiveContent:
Which return statement executes in this case?

The last return statementThe first return statement

The last return statement.
lessons.hardModeContent:
For the displayed call getDiscount(28), neither condition is true. What is logged?

Full price25% OFF25%

Make sure to pick Full price.

lessons.title: Example: End of a function
lessons.interactiveContent:
Return number * 10 for this function.

Make sure to type return.

lessons.title: Example: Nothing gets executed
lessons.interactiveContent:
Display only Math started by coding the messages in their correct positions.

Make sure to pick "Math started", followed by "Math is done!".
lessons.hardModeContent:
A return statement exits the function, so statements after it do not run.

Display Math started, then return the multiplication result 300.

Make sure to pick "Math started", followed by return, and finally number * 10.

lessons.title: Example: Multiple return statements
lessons.interactiveContent:
Return the multiplication result by placing the return statements in their correct positions.

Make sure to pick return number * 10;, followed by return "Math started";.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Complete two return statements: first return the multiplication result 300, then the string Math started.

Make sure to pick return, followed by number * 10, return, and finally "Math started".

lessons.title: Example: Last return statements
lessons.interactiveContent:
Display the message "Without honors" by placing the return statements in their correct positions.

Make sure to pick return "With honors";, followed by return "Without honors";.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Return With honors for grades of at least 75, and Without honors otherwise.

Make sure to pick return, followed by "With honors", return, and finally "Without honors".

lessons.title: Example: Return in if statements
lessons.interactiveContent:
Display the message With honors by coding the right value.

Make sure to pick 98.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Return With honors for grades of at least 75. Complete the condition and test it with 98.

Make sure to pick >=, followed by 75, and finally 98.

lessons.title: Example: Catch last case
lessons.interactiveContent:
Execute the last return statement by coding the correct value.

Make sure to pick 95.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Return Too cold below 95, and Too hot above 95.

Complete both comparisons and choose an input that returns Just right.

Make sure to pick <, followed by >, and finally 95.
